seo.description: Fit-only large format porcelain tiling in Sunningdale. Flat substrates, full adhesive coverage, lippage-free finish for period and modern homes. From £3,500.

h1: Large format porcelain tiling in Sunningdale

hero.intro: Sunningdale is best known for the golf courses that share its name and the large detached properties around them — a mix of Victorian and Edwardian houses, inter-war family homes and more recent executive-style builds, often on private or gated roads. That spread of property ages matters to us before we tile a single slab: a Victorian or Edwardian suspended timber floor behaves very differently under a rigid porcelain slab than a modern concrete subfloor does, and we check which we're dealing with at survey stage. We work fit-only, from £3,500, with you sourcing the tiles, sanitaryware, brassware and furniture.

sections.heading: Older timber floors need different substrate prep
sections.body: A number of the Victorian and Edwardian houses we see in Sunningdale have suspended timber floors rather than solid concrete, and timber flexes under load in a way that a rigid, low-flex porcelain slab doesn't tolerate well. Left unaddressed, that flex is what causes grout lines to crack and, in the worst cases, the tile itself to fracture. Where we find a timber subfloor, we overboard it with a rigid backer board system designed to reduce deflection before any adhesive goes down — it's an extra step, but it's the difference between a floor that lasts and one that cracks within a year.

sections.heading: Generous plots give us room to move the layout
sections.body: The plot sizes around Sunningdale tend to be larger than a terraced or semi-detached property would offer, and that generally gives us more flexibility on layout — moving a waste run three feet to accommodate a freestanding bath, for example, is rarely blocked by a neighbouring structural wall the way it would be in a tighter property. Where a layout changes, the new floor area gets the same flatness check and full adhesive bed as the rest of the room, regardless of whether it's new build or a reworked corner of a period house.

sections.heading: Full-bed adhesive and lippage control on every slab
sections.body: Large format porcelain needs full adhesive coverage across the entire back of the slab, not a few dabs or a perimeter bead, because any gap underneath becomes a weak spot under standing load. We comb adhesive onto the substrate and back-butter the slab itself, then use levelling clips through the run so each slab edge sits flush with its neighbour — avoiding the lippage that catches light unevenly and the dirt that collects in a slightly proud edge.

sections.heading: Book a survey before you order tiles
sections.body: We start with a paid £125 survey so we can check whether your subfloor is timber or solid, assess the layout, and tell you what the installation will need before you commit to a tile order. Call or WhatsApp 07399 651836 to arrange a Sunningdale survey.

faqs.q: Can large format porcelain go over a timber floor?
faqs.a: Yes, but it needs the right preparation — typically a rigid backer board system to reduce deflection, since timber floors flex more than a rigid porcelain slab can tolerate without cracking.

faqs.q: How do you know if my floor is timber or solid before the survey?
faqs.a: We check at survey — older Victorian and Edwardian properties in the Sunningdale area are more likely to have suspended timber floors, while newer builds are more often solid concrete, but we confirm it on-site rather than assume.

faqs.q: Can you move my bath or shower to a different wall?
faqs.a: Often, yes — the larger plots common around Sunningdale tend to give us more room to reroute waste pipes than a smaller property would, though it depends on what the survey finds.

faqs.q: What does fit-only mean for a Sunningdale installation?
faqs.a: You buy the sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture; we handle strip-out, first-fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging, from £3,500.

faqs.q: Why do you charge for a survey?
faqs.a: The £125 survey lets us properly check the substrate, access and layout before you buy tiles, so you're not ordering based on guesswork.
